# Classroom with weekly quizzes

Simulate a six-week course with one teacher and five students, all AI agents. The course covers three topics: fractions, decimals and percentages. Every week the teacher chooses one topic to teach, and each student chooses whether to study hard or take it easy that week. A student's understanding of a topic grows when it is taught and grows more when they study. At the end of every week there is a quiz on that week's topic, scored from 0 to 10, based on the student's understanding of the topic plus some luck. Students see only their own quiz scores; the teacher sees everyone's. A student's final grade is the average of their quiz scores.

## Deliverables

Report these outputs:
- `quiz_scores` — a map from each student's id to the list of their quiz scores, one per week in order.
- `final_grades` — a map from each student's id to their final grade.
- `class_average` — the average of the final grades.


Build this environment. Save it with write_contract and use the other tools as you see fit. Reply without calling a tool when you are done.
I'll start by reading the guide parts I need.
I'll design the contract now, then check it.

Understanding of a topic grows by {$inputs.base_gain} when it is taught, plus {$inputs.study_gain} more when the student studies hard. Then there is a quiz on that week's topic: 0 to {$inputs.max_score}, based on understanding plus up to {+/-}{$inputs.luck_range} of luck. Students see only their own scores; the teacher sees everyone's. A final grade is the average of a student's quiz scores.

BRIEF:
# Classroom with weekly quizzes
A class of 5 students takes a 6-week course with one teacher. The course covers fractions, decimals, percentages.

## Rules
Every week the teacher picks one topic to teach and each student privately decides whether to study hard or take it easy. Understanding of a topic grows by 2 when it is taught, plus 2 more when the student studies hard. Then there is a quiz on that week's topic: 0 to 10, based on understanding plus or minus up to 2 of luck. Students see only their own scores; the teacher sees everyone's. A final grade is the average of a student's quiz scores.

## You
You are Teacher (teacher, id teacher_1).
You see every student's quiz scores. Each week choose the topic to teach.
Act only through your tools. Your turn ends when you take a final action or call end_turn.

Now: It is your turn.

- end_turn: Finish your turn. {"type": "object", "properties": {}, "additionalProperties": false}

BRIEF:
# Classroom with weekly quizzes
A class of 5 students takes a 6-week course with one teacher. The course covers fractions, decimals, percentages.

## Rules
Every week the teacher picks one topic to teach and each student privately decides whether to study hard or take it easy. Understanding of a topic grows by 2 when it is taught, plus 2 more when the student studies hard. Then there is a quiz on that week's topic: 0 to 10, based on understanding plus or minus up to 2 of luck. Students see only their own scores; the teacher sees everyone's. A final grade is the average of a student's quiz scores.

## You
You are Student 1 (student, id student_1).
You see your own quiz scores and the topic taught. Each week choose to study hard or take it easy.
Act only through your tools. Your turn ends when you take a final action or call end_turn.

UPDATE:
Week 1 of 6 · study
Now: Everyone chooses at the same time.

Since your last turn:
- This week's topic is percentages.

This week's topic is percentages. Your quiz scores so far: .

TOOLS:
- effort: Choose whether to study hard or take it easy this week. (Committed when everyone has chosen.) {"type": "object", "properties": {"level": {"enum": ["hard", "easy"], "type": "string", "description": "hard: study hard; easy: take it easy."}}, "additionalProperties": false, "required": ["level"]}
- inspect: Details of one entity by its id (shown in [brackets] after names). Free: up to 8 reads (looks and inspects) per turn do not use a tool call. {"type": "object", "properties": {"id": {"type": "string", "enum": ["student_1"]}}, "required": ["id"], "additionalProperties": false}
- end_turn: Finish your turn (your choices are submitted). {"type": "object", "properties": {}, "additionalProperties": false}

The check is clean, previews match the brief exactly, and the seeded hand-check confirms the mechanics.

Verification: with `teacher: policy:rotate` (fractions→decimals→percentages, repeating) and every student on `policy:grind` (studies hard each week), each student gains 4 understanding in the taught topic per week. For `student_1`, the run gives `[2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 9]` — i.e. understanding 4 with luck −2 at week 1, then 4, 4, 8, 8, 8 with luck −1, 0, −1, 0, +1. Quiz scores stay in 0–10, the final grade is the mean of the six scores (`33/6 = 5.5`), and `class_average = 5.7333`. That is exactly what the brief implies.

The contract `Classroom with weekly quizzes`:
- **Clock** 6 weeks of one round each, with inputs defaulting to the brief's numbers (`weeks` 6, `students` 5, three topics, gains 2 + 2, score bound 10, luck ±2).
- **Two agent types**: one `teacher` (sees the whole `quiz_board` of everyone's scores) and `student`s (see only their own `my_scores`), each with private per-topic `understanding`, their `scores` list and this week's `effort`.
- **Stages**: a sequential `lesson` where the teacher picks the topic, then a simultaneous `study` stage so students' hard/easy choices are sealed and committed together (their `effort` is a private action, so no one else learns it).
- **End-of-week event**: every student's understanding of the taught topic rises by the base gain (plus the study gain if they studied hard, capped at 10), then a quiz of understanding ± luck, rounded and clamped to 0–10, is appended to their scores.
- **Outputs** under the brief's names: `quiz_scores` (id → per-week list), `final_grades` (id → mean score) and `class_average`, with invariants keeping scores and understanding in range.

Done.
